title: Boards of abstract names
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, before any computation and before ticket B's census. Names are a countable set with no letters; a state gives each pair of names a neighbour distinction and each name a value; a uniform law treats all names alike. To be proved: (T1) every finitary law that allows a state allows one with constant adjacency and values (Ramsey), so no finitary law forces a neighbour, bounded degree needs a forbidden homogeneous star, and no finitary law forces a finite board other than one place; (T2) with existence clauses giving every place exactly 2k neighbours, every board is a disjoint union of Schreier graphs of F_k; (T3) a count law allows the universal cover of every component of an allowed board; (T4) no first-order law forces connected boards when a board has a component of infinite diameter, and a named square with coordinates mod 3 and an aperiodic tile set makes every component a plane; (T5) in a count law, edges with the same pair of values can exchange partners and far places of different value can exchange names, so every neighbour distinction and value is flipped by a finite change. Each target is proved, refuted, or left with its gap stated.
failure_conditions: A finitary law with an allowed state and no state of constant adjacency and values (against T1).
A countable 2k-regular simple graph with no decomposition into k oriented 2-factors (against T2).
A count law with a board containing a cycle and no tree board (against T3, and A54 overturned).
A first-order law all of whose boards are connected while one has a component of infinite diameter (against T4).
A count-law state in which the switch or the swap breaks the law (against T5).
remaining_obligations: Targets T1 to T5, or the record of which fails and why
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of neighbour distinctions on a countable set of names with no letters; uniform laws over finite alphabets, finitary or with existence clauses. Neighbour distinctions are distinctions of the law, never contact by themselves (A51).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10.
validation.status: pre-registered; the proof attempt to follow
